LESSON: INDICES AND LOGARITHMS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: NUMBERS 1.2 Cubes and Cube Roots (5 lessons) By the end of the sub-strand, the l
Topic 1.3: Indices and Logarithms
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Indices and Logarithms, part of NUMBERS 1.2 Cubes and Cube Roots (5 lessons) By the end of the sub-strand, the l in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do we express numbers in power form?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to indices and logarithms,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. express numbers in index form in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. derive the laws of indices in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. apply the laws of indices in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. relate powers of 10 to common logarithms in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. reflect on use of indices and logarithms in real life situations. ● In pairs, learners are guided to sign terms such as indices, logarithms, laws of indices, power, base. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to discuss and relate powers to indices and identify the base. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to show how to derive the laws of indices using multiplication and division. ● In groups, learners are guided to use the laws of indices to work out indices. ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to discuss and relate powers of 10 to common logarithms. ● In groups, learners are guided to use digital devices or other resources to work out common logarithms. How do we express numbers in power form? 8

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Indices and Logarithms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Understands and respects diversity and contributes to group decision making; A learner

recognizes the value of others’ ideas as they discuss how to use indices and logarithms of numbers.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: Imagines different situations; A learner develops open mindedness and creativity as

they generate and show the laws of indices using multiplication and division.

Values:
● Responsibility: A learner enhances diligence as they use digital devices such as calculators or other resources to work out

indices and logarithms of numbers.

● Unity: A learner enriches cooperation as they work in groups during the discussion on indices and logarithms of numbers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Citizenship Education: A learner promotes equity as they use multiplication and division and relate to fair sharing of resources.

Link to other learning areas:

● The learner is able to relate the skill of multiplication and division taught in mathematics to calculations in Pre-technical

Studies.

Suggested resource

● Mathematical tables, Calculators.
